name: Strikeshield Dynamics BDA-9 Blast Disposal Suit
description:
Bulky, olive-drab full-body blast attenuation suit with articulated composite panels over a shear-thickening fluid underlayer. The outer shell is matte-finished boron carbide over polycarbonate, with a distinctive quilted appearance from the fluid-pack underlayer beneath. Helmet is integrated, full-face, with heads-up display and filtered external audio. Weighs 34 kilograms unassisted.

Most BDA-9 wearers use a lightweight servo-assist undersuit — sold separately. The suit accommodates spinal rigs and neural ports but requires pre-fitting for any significant chrome augmentation. Tier 3-4 municipal bomb disposal units use it; black-market versions stripped of the tracking transponder show up occasionally on Shelf fixers.
functionality: Rated for fragmentation and overpressure up to 15kg TNT equivalent at 3-meter standoff. Shear-thickening fluid layer hardens on impact. Integrated HUD displays threat-assessment BCI feed and structural integrity sensors. Filtered audio allows communication while muffling blast wave. Transponder logs location and suit integrity data to central dispatch in real time.
what_it_says: Someone decided your life is worth more than the cost of this suit — or you stole it because you had no choice.
story_hooks: A BDA-9 with its transponder removed turned up on a Shelf fixer — the suit's integrity log still contains encrypted data from its last authorized deployment, and someone wants it erased.
A Tier 3 disposal tech discovers her suit's real-time location feed has been accessed by a private corponation account, not her employer — she's been surveilled on every job for two years.
The shear-thickening fluid in a batch of BDA-9 suits has been diluted during manufacture; the suits will pass visual inspection but fail under live blast conditions.

physical_description.visual_profile: A heavily armored, utilitarian silhouette that dominates the wearer's frame. The suit reads as industrial and purposeful — broad-shouldered, chunky through the torso, with segmented limbs that telegraph protection over mobility. The integrated helmet creates an imposing, faceless presence. Visual impression: municipal worker, hazmat operative, or military ordnance specialist.
physical_description.fit: Oversized and deliberately bulky, designed for layering over a servo-assist undersuit. Articulated at joints to allow movement despite weight. Compression-fit at wrists, ankles, and neck seals. The suit accommodates augmented personnel but requires custom fitting for significant chrome.
physical_description.primary_material: Outer shell: matte boron carbide composite over polycarbonate backing. Underlayer: shear-thickening non-Newtonian fluid in segmented packs. Jointing: flexible reinforced synthetic polymer with friction-bonded articulation plates.
physical_description.texture: Distinctively quilted surface appearance from the pressurized fluid packs beneath the rigid outer shell. The boron carbide has a slightly pebbly, non-reflective matte finish. Seams are reinforced and visible. Overall tactile impression: industrial, deliberately engineered, not designed for comfort.
physical_description.color_scheme: Olive-drab green as primary, with matte black reinforcement panels at high-stress points (shoulders, elbows, knees, spine). Minimal branding — small Strikeshield Dynamics logo on left chest. Faint wear patterns on knees and forearms from repeated deployment.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty magnetic snap chest plate, friction-fit helmet with integrated locking collar, friction-bonded side panels with emergency rip-points. Sealed wrist and ankle cuffs with micro-lock toggles.
distinctive_features: Integrated full-face helmet with heads-up display and filtered external audio system
Quilted surface from underlying shear-thickening fluid compartments
Articulated composite panel system at all major joints
Spinal mount points for neural rigs and ports
Removable tracking transponder (factory-standard, often stripped on black-market variants)
Reinforced blast-attenuation paneling across chest, back, and abdomen
Heavy-duty service loops and gear attachment points at waist and thighs
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 municipal/contractor — expensive equipment for working-class hazmat and bomb disposal personnel. Signals official sanction, training, and access to corpo resources. Black-market stripped versions indicate Tier 4-5 street operators using salvaged/stolen gear.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is either a licensed municipal disposal technician (corpo-aligned) or a dangerous improviser using military-grade protection for subversive purposes. The suit says 'trained, equipped, and authorized' — or 'desperate enough to steal one.' Either way: somebody dealing with ordnance, explosives, or extreme hazard environments.
physical_description.condition_typical: Professionally maintained units show minimal wear; scuffed matte finish, minor dents in boron carbide panels, faint chemical stains on lower sections. Black-market versions often show signs of transponder removal (crude gouges on left shoulder), patched fluid leaks, or makeshift reinforcements. Never pristine.

image_prompt: A muscular, augmented neo-noir model wearing the BDA-9 Blast Disposal Suit in olive drab, standing in a dark industrial warehouse with flickering blue neon overhead. The suit's quilted surface and boron carbide plating catch harsh sidelighting. Full integrated helmet with faint HUD glow visible through the faceplate. Minimal background detail — concrete, shadow, one warning light flashing red. Shot from low angle to emphasize bulk and imposing silhouette. Moody, utilitarian, official-but-worn aesthetic. --ar 2:3 --v 6
